verdict: Sound for the audited local HSConfig source-contract logic. The implementation now separates true Hearthstone semantics from runtime-write authority: start-of-game effects, hero power transforms, deckbuilding/start-in-deck facts, broad guide text, and card importance do not become Mulligan.json keeps unless they arrive as exact, surface-eligible mulligan_keep claims and pass the Mulligan surface gate. Explicit mulligan_discard can lower to the Mulligan surface, but discard is not inferred from absent keep text. The remaining risk is not a broad architectural flaw; it is a coverage and ingress risk when a source path mislabels vague text as exact mulligan_keep or reaches build_mulligan_plan without the card_roles and semantic_families needed to suppress non-hand start-of-game effects.

evidence_sources.evidence: The operator guide states that runtime Mulligan writes require explicit mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard claim_kind values, while card importance, start-of-game effects, deckbuilding effects, hero-power-transform text, and guide gameplan text remain contract evidence unless separately backed by exact hand-required Mulligan guidance. It also keeps source_contract_audit.json diagnostic and operator_summary.json as the normal apply authority.

The guide policy says source truth is not runtime authority. Runtime lowering is surface-gated: Mulligan.json only lowers explicit mulligan_keep or mulligan_discard, GlobalValues.json only lowers runtime-lowerable gameplan_posture, Combo.json only lowers complete combo_sequence, and per-card CardID JSON only lowers supported CardID behavior claim kinds. It explicitly bans inferring mulligan_keep from card importance, start-of-game effects, deckbuilding effects, hero-power-transform text, or generic keep wording.

SUPPORTED_ATOMIC_CLAIM_KINDS separates mulligan_keep, mulligan_discard, hero_power_transform, card_role, targeting_rule, combo_sequence, gameplan_posture, and choice claims. MULLIGAN_SURFACE_CLAIM_KINDS is limited to mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard. can_lower_to_mulligan rejects non-mulligan claim kinds, rejects non-runtime-lowerable claims, and rejects mulligan_keep for start-of-game non-hand effects with reason start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand.

The policy matrix classifies mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard as runtime_lowerable only on the mulligan surface. hero_power_transform is suppressed_or_conditional with allowed surface cardid and an operator meaning that it preserves hero-power-transform semantics without being a mulligan keep by itself.

build_mulligan_plan calls can_lower_to_mulligan for every claim before producing hold or discard rules. Rejected claims are recorded in suppressed_rules with the gate reason. The quality block marks Mulligan richness as thin when there are no source-backed keeps instead of inventing holds.

Both contract builders derive mulligan_anchor only from runtime_claim_kind(claim) == mulligan_keep and negative-keep checks. Generic pressure, combo, hero-power, or broad guide text can become usage expectations or roles, but they do not become hold intent unless the normalized runtime claim kind is an exact Mulligan keep.

Static semantics and enrichment identify start_of_game and Shadowform/hero_power_transform families, and semantic enrichment preserves hero-power-transform meaning through linked hero-power/deckwide-effect data instead of requiring opening-hand retention.

Regression tests show broad legacy mulligan_and_gameplan text does not create hold rules, exact legacy mulligan_keep still creates runtime authority, runtime_claim_kind maps only exact legacy runtime types, hero_power_transform does not lower to Mulligan, hero_power_transform can emit a CardID behavior row without Mulligan keep, broad keep text stays non-mulligan runtime, explicit start-of-game keeps are suppressed, non-hand start-of-game roles suppress keeps, and start_of_game plus mulligan_anchor remains allowed.

ShadowPriest fixture tests assert Darkbishop Benedictus has hero_power_transform evidence but no mulligan_keep claim, and a synthetic start-of-game hero-power-transform keep claim is suppressed with reason start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand.

Surface-authority tests freeze the split between source claim kinds and runtime surfaces, including hero_power_transform not being a mulligan keep and policy rows matching surface-gate decisions. Source-contract spine freeze tests protect claim-kind policy from drift.

Source document building records readiness, trust ceiling, source confidence, specificity status, runtime_lowerable status, and opposing mulligan keep/discard conflicts. The evidence verifier warns on unsupported runtime blocks, low-confidence runtime lowering, and runtime-lowering hints that lack actionable specificity.

current_strengths.detail: Mulligan runtime authority is keyed to exact mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard claim kinds, not to free-text mentions of keep, important, pressure, start of game, or hero power.

The source_document_model gate rejects wrong-surface claims before builders emit runtime rows. A true hero_power_transform claim can be preserved on a CardID behavior surface while being rejected from the Mulligan surface.

The Mulligan gate suppresses start-of-game non-hand effects, deck-state modifiers, deckbuilding modifiers, deck-size/even-odd/highlander modifiers, hero-power transforms, passive start effects, and start-in-deck requirements unless the card also carries a valid mulligan_anchor.

Tests cover legacy broad mulligan_and_gameplan claims and broad keep wording so those paths do not silently create opening-hand holds. Exact legacy mulligan_keep remains supported only because it is an intentional compatibility path.

Static semantics and semantic enrichment keep start-of-game and hero-power-transform meaning visible in reports, deckwide effects, and CardID behavior planning. This avoids the old failure mode where removing a Mulligan hold also erased the effect.

current_strengths.strength: Mulligan thinness is reported instead of patched with guesses
current_strengths.detail: build_mulligan_plan marks no_source_backed_mulligan_keeps and thin status when explicit keep evidence is missing. It does not fabricate holds from card importance or early-game role.
mulligan_discard lowers to the Mulligan surface when explicitly claimed, while absent keep text and negative wording do not automatically become runtime discard rows.

current_strengths.strength: Diagnostics do not become apply gates
current_strengths.detail: source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, contract_spine_rows, and source-quality summaries explain decisions without replacing operator_summary.json as the single normal apply authority.

current_strengths.strength: Regression coverage matches the known Darkbishop failure mode
current_strengths.detail: Tests assert the Darkbishop Benedictus split directly: hero_power_transform evidence remains present while SW_448 is absent from Mulligan holds unless a valid hand-retention claim survives the surface gate.

gaps_or_risks.detail: The start-of-game suppression depends on card_roles and semantic_families being available to can_lower_to_mulligan. A direct expert or legacy path that passes a mislabeled exact mulligan_keep with empty card_roles can bypass the non-hand-effect check because the gate cannot see the start_of_game role.

The system intentionally trusts exact mulligan_keep for compatibility. If a source author or importer labels broad importance text as exact mulligan_keep, HSConfig will treat it as runtime authority unless another guard such as start-of-game suppression, confidence/readiness, selector validation, or conflict handling rejects it.

gaps_or_risks.risk: Deckbuilding and passive-start coverage depends on semantic naming
gaps_or_risks.detail: The suppression table covers known role names such as deckbuilding_modifier, start_in_deck_requirement, highlander_modifier, even_odd_modifier, and passive_start_effect. New Hearthstone mechanics or alternate metadata labels can remain report-only or partially visible until mapped into these semantic families.

gaps_or_risks.risk: Card importance can still seek CardID lowering
gaps_or_risks.detail: Card_role, targeting_rule, mechanic_usage, and hero_power_transform can be runtime_lowerable on CardID surfaces when they have supported blocks. Weak card-importance text with a runtime_block hint can still create pressure for behavior lowering, so specificity warnings and supported-block checks must stay visible.

The current policy correctly avoids inferring discard from absent keep text, but negative keep phrases become avoid/usage expectations unless encoded as mulligan_discard. This is safe against false lowering, but it can leave real discard advice report-only when source documents are not explicit.

gaps_or_risks.risk: Hero power transform lowering needs identity and block support
gaps_or_risks.detail: hero_power_transform is allowed on the CardID surface only when the behavior can be represented by documented blocks such as BeforeUseHeroPowerBonus. Unresolved transformed hero powers, generated entities, or unsupported hero-power timing should remain suppressed/report-only rather than become guessed runtime rows.

gaps_or_risks.risk: Conflicts are only as useful as their reporting path
gaps_or_risks.detail: Opposing mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard claims are detected in source_document_builder, but operators still need those conflicts surfaced in the normal package reports so they do not mistake a valid load-safe package for source-backed strong.

gaps_or_risks.risk: Future mechanics can create false confidence
gaps_or_risks.detail: Unknown or warning-only mechanics are meant to stay descriptive and non-blocking. If a future mechanic resembles a start-of-game or deckbuilding modifier but is only detected as generic text, it may not receive the stronger non-hand suppression reason until mapped.

recommended_next_actions.action: Add a normal-path regression fixture for role-context ingress
recommended_next_actions.detail: Run the normal prepare/research-contract path with a start-of-game or deckbuilding card that is deliberately mislabelled as mulligan_keep, then assert no Mulligan.json hold is emitted, source_contract_audit records start_of_game_effect_does_not_require_opening_hand, and the effect remains visible in semantic/card behavior reports.

recommended_next_actions.action: Add a warning-only source lint for suspicious exact keeps
recommended_next_actions.detail: When claim_kind is mulligan_keep but evidence text lacks explicit opening-hand language and the card carries start_of_game, deckbuilding, hero_power_transform, passive-start, or pure importance roles, emit a warning in source evidence or source claim quality reports. Keep it non-blocking.

recommended_next_actions.action: Keep the non-hand-effect role table under fixture coverage
recommended_next_actions.detail: For each role in START_OF_GAME_NON_HAND_EFFECT_ROLES, keep or add a parameterized test that proves exact mulligan_keep is suppressed unless the card also has a valid mulligan_anchor. Extend the table when static_semantics or semantic_enrichment introduces a new equivalent role.

recommended_next_actions.action: Preserve the Darkbishop split as a control case
recommended_next_actions.detail: Keep a fixture-level assertion that SW_448 can preserve hero_power_transform and Mind Spike/Shadowform behavior while staying absent from Mulligan holds. This is the clearest end-to-end guard against the original false-runtime-claim regression.

recommended_next_actions.action: Treat exact discard as a source authoring requirement
recommended_next_actions.detail: Do not infer mulligan_discard from absent keep text. Instead, have source_claim_gap_report or source_claim_quality_summary request explicit mulligan_discard evidence when the guide implies a throw but does not provide a structured discard claim.

recommended_next_actions.action: Run contract-spine and surface authority tests on contract changes
recommended_next_actions.detail: For changes touching source_document_model.py, source_contract_matrix.py, mulligan_plan.py, guide importers, static semantics, or semantic enrichment, run the claim-kind runtime contract tests, surface authority split tests, source contract spine freeze tests, and the Darkbishop fixture tests.

For card importance, hero-power, discover, choose-one, generated-entity, and targeting claims, require supported runtime_block and resolved identity before emitting per-card JSON. Otherwise keep the claim in suppression/report-only diagnostics with the first missing link.

no_blocking_constraints.constraint: Do not add a second apply gate
no_blocking_constraints.detail: source_contract_audit.json, source_to_runtime_explainability.json, contract_spine_rows, source claim quality reports, and semantic drift reports must remain diagnostics. operator_summary.json remains the only normal apply authority.

no_blocking_constraints.constraint: Do not block load-safe packages for thin Mulligan evidence
no_blocking_constraints.detail: A present but thin Mulligan.json is a source-depth and usefulness signal, not a HearthRanger load-safety error. Keep the package valid when technical_status is VALID_PACKAGE and report the missing source-backed keep/discard evidence as follow-up work.

no_blocking_constraints.constraint: Do not invent runtime rows from true but wrong-surface facts
no_blocking_constraints.detail: Start-of-game effects, deckbuilding requirements, hero-power transforms, card importance, broad guide gameplans, report-only mechanics, unresolved generated entities, and unsupported blocks must remain visible as contract evidence or suppressed diagnostics unless a documented matching runtime surface exists.

Mulligan.json accepts only mulligan_keep and mulligan_discard. GlobalValues.json accepts only source-backed Step 1 gameplan_posture overlays. Combo.json requires complete combo_sequence data. CardID JSON requires supported block and identity.
Do not use replay results, winrate, runtime logs, or after-game tuning to justify source-contract lowering. Runtime-evidence-required tuning belongs outside this pre-run contract path.

no_blocking_constraints.constraint: Preserve effect visibility when suppressing false keeps
no_blocking_constraints.detail: When a Mulligan keep is suppressed because the card is a start-of-game or hero-power-transform enabler, keep the semantic effect visible in reports and supported CardID behavior output instead of deleting the effect from the package.

Low-confidence runtime lowering, warning-only mechanics, unresolved option identity, unsupported conditions, and future mechanic drift should point to next inspection steps without preventing autonomous generation of a technically valid load-safe package.
